company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS at $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point gross margin tailwind from tariff refunds and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% versus expectations of +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year over year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex more aggressively in the Physical AI and robotics perception space.

MillerKnoll posted solid FQ1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, implying organic EPS of 42 cents. Sales disappointed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million versus the $943.2 million consensus, though orders rose 3.5% year over year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed to $3.88–4.03 billion from $3.93–4.13 billion, while the EPS range of $1.85–2.15 was left unchanged.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The leadership change is an incremental organizational update with no financial guidance revision attached.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, as gross margins fell 230 basis points year over year to 12.4% versus the 13.85% estimate, though revenue of $2.311 billion edged above the $2.17 billion consensus. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure weighing on household budgets and retail, and rising material costs pressuring margins. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, ongoing structural cost actions, and a roughly 75% surge in North American towable RV order backlog year over year, though the company declined to issue formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after the company reported positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. The data represent a meaningful read on the drug's efficacy and competitive positioning within the crowded but high-growth GLP-1 obesity therapy market. The positive results are a significant catalyst for the stock.

tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd, covering six names reporting before the open. There is no broad macro or rates commentary in this edition — let's go straight to the names.

Starting with AutoZone. The company beat fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share at $56.05 versus the Street at $54.03, but the quality of that beat is a real concern. The upside was driven by tariff refunds adding 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash LIFO benefit adding another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture is weaker — domestic comps came in at only plus 1.6% versus expectations of plus 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year over year. Management did point to improving sales trends in the back half of the quarter, but this is a mixed print at best.

Cognex is making a significant acquisition, buying RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI — for roughly $500 million upfront plus an additional $106 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80 to $90 million in revenue growing more than 50% year over year. This is a strategically aggressive move into the Physical AI and robotics space and reads as a bullish signal for Cognex's long-term positioning.

MillerKnoll beat fiscal first quarter earnings per share at 53 cents versus 36 cents expected, and importantly, even backing out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, they still would have beaten at 42 cents. That's a clean beat. Sales were light though, down 3.3% organically to $923 million versus $943 million expected. Full-year sales guidance was trimmed modestly while the earnings per share range held. A mixed print — better quality than it looks on the surface, but top-line pressure is real.

Pentair named a new permanent CFO, Bob Hau, effective November 1st. Hau has prior CFO experience at three well-known industrial companies. No guidance changes attached — this is a straightforward leadership transition.

THOR Industries missed fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share at 78 cents versus 87 cents expected. Gross margins fell 230 basis points year over year to 12.4% versus nearly 14% expected. Management was candid about the headwinds — interest rates, fuel costs, inflation squeezing household budgets, and rising material costs hitting margins. The company sees a relatively flat retail sales environment ahead and won't give formal guidance until later in the fall. There were some positives — dealer inventory is healthy, structural cost actions are underway, and North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year over year. But the headline print and tone are bearish.

Finally, the standout mover this morning is Viking Therapeutics. Shares are spiking pre-market after the company reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 weight loss drug, showing 22% weight loss. That is a compelling efficacy read in a market that is intensely focused on this therapeutic category. This is a clear bullish catalyst and will likely be one of the most active trades of the day.

No macro, no Fed commentary today — this is a pure earnings and catalyst morning. Watch Viking closely at the open, and be cautious on AutoZone given the low quality of the beat.
